# a5pyramid

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5pyramid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5pyramid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/belian-earth/a5pyramid/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/belian-earth/a5pyramid)
[![extendr](https://img.shields.io/badge/extendr-^0.9.0-276DC2)](https://extendr.rs/extendr/extendr_api/)
<!-- badges: end -->

a5pyramid builds level-of-detail pyramids of [A5](https://a5geo.org/)
cells and writes them, with the cells they summarise, to one Parquet file
laid out for the browser. A web map reads the file's footer, picks the
level for its zoom and fetches only the tiles in view with HTTP range
requests, for example with [hyparquet](https://github.com/hyparam/hyparquet)
and deck.gl. No tile server and no pre-cut tile directory are needed: one
static file serves every zoom.

It takes cells from [a5R](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5R) and
[a5px](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5px), and replaces the pyramid
builder in [a5view](https://github.com/belian-earth/a5view). The engine is a
Rust crate with no R dependency, in `src/rust/a5pyramid`, to be published
on its own.

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | `a5_pyramid()` builds the levels as a tibble; `a5_write_pyramid()` builds and writes them to Parquet in Rust, in parallel |
| Reduce | mean, sum, min, max, mode, or a representative leaf that keeps real combinations of values such as colours |
| Read | `a5_pyramid_info()` reads the index from the footer; `a5_read_pyramid()` reads levels within a bounding box, as a renderer does |
| Format | One row group per tile, with each tile's level and bounding box indexed in the file's metadata; specified in [`FORMAT.md`](src/rust/a5pyramid/FORMAT.md) |

## Installation

a5pyramid is not on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("belian-earth/a5pyramid")
```

Building from source needs a [Rust toolchain](https://rustup.rs/) with
`rustc` 1.88 or later.

## Example

`s2_santiago`, from a5view, holds 15,626 resolution-18 cells (about 22 m
across) of a cloud-free Sentinel-2 mosaic over Santiago, Chile, with the
blue, green, red and near-infrared bands. This writes a pyramid of it with a
representative leaf for the bands, so a coarse cell keeps the colour of a
real pixel rather than a blend, and the mean NDVI.

```{r write, message = FALSE}
library(a5pyramid)

santiago <- a5view::s2_santiago
santiago$ndvi <- with(santiago, (B08 - B04) / (B08 + B04))

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
a5_write_pyramid(
  santiago, path,
  aggregate = "rep_child",
  reducers = c(ndvi = "mean"),
  types = c(B02 = "uint16", B03 = "uint16", B04 = "uint16", B08 = "uint16", ndvi = "float32")
)
```

```{r info}
a5_pyramid_info(path)
```

Every coarser level groups the leaves by the cell containing their centres,
so each level partitions the data and `ncell` counts the leaves under each
cell. A browser opening the file reads the footer only, here a few
kilobytes, and then the tiles it draws. `a5_read_pyramid()` reads levels the
same way:

```{r levels, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 120}
library(ggplot2)

levels <- a5_read_pyramid(path, lod = c(14, 16, 18))
ggplot(levels, aes(cell = cell, fill = a5view::cells_rgb(B04, B03, B02, range = c(300, 2800)))) +
  a5view::geom_a5() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("LOD", lod)) +
  theme_void()
```

## How it works

**Levels.** A cell at LOD `r` summarises the leaves whose centres it
contains (`a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell()`). Supercells do not chain: a leaf's
supercell two resolutions up is often not the supercell of its supercell one
resolution up, so every level is grouped from the leaves directly.

**Tiles.** Each level is split into tiles of at most `tile_size` rows, one
Parquet row group each. A tile is a run of consecutive cell ids, and A5 ids
follow a space-filling curve, so a run is a compact patch of the globe.
Levels are split down the A5 hierarchy only where a run holds more cells than
fit a tile, so tiles are coarse where data is sparse and fine where it is
dense, and every level stays sorted by cell id.

**Index.** The file's key-value metadata holds a JSON index of the levels,
the value columns, and the bounding box of every row group, computed from
the cells' boundaries (antimeridian and poles included). Cell ids are delta
encoded, which takes them from 8 bytes per row to about 3, and Snappy
compression keeps the file readable by hyparquet with no extra libraries.
The test suite reads files with hyparquet under Node and checks that only
the footer and the requested row group are fetched.

## Performance

Writing a pyramid of 439,276 resolution-16 cells over central Scotland,
with four `uint8` colour channels and a `float32` value, as a5view prepares
them (`benchmarks/bench-vs-a5view.R`, 20 threads):

| | a5view 0.3 | a5pyramid |
|---|---|---|
| mean | 4.06 s | 0.48 s |
| rep_child | 4.06 s | 0.49 s |
| file size | 9.0 MB | 6.5 MB |

Both spend most of their single-threaded time in the a5 crate's supercell
lookup; a5pyramid gains by running it in parallel and by building the
levels and the file without R in between. Results do not depend on the
number of threads, which `a5pyramid_threads()` sets.
